# S2 — Cap Docker overlay2 and BuildKit cache with per-generator alarms

## Why
ADR 0112 decisions 1+2, for the Docker accumulator. At the 2026-09-02 outage
`/var/lib/docker` was 17G (overlay2 16G across 67 layer dirs) while `docker system df`
claimed ~9.5 GB with ZERO dangling images — roughly **6.5 GB of orphaned overlay2 was
invisible to `docker prune` entirely**. Four rounds of prune reclaimed ~1.06 GB against a
29 GB problem. So a cap that reads Docker's own accounting cannot see the bytes that caused
the outage, and today's prune logic is reactive with no ceiling.

## Design

### One budget, measured from the filesystem — not from Docker's ledger
`infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh` (new) is the single source of truth for a
`/var/lib/docker` budget with an internal split (ADR 0112: "S2 and S5 are one budget, not
two" — writable layers live INSIDE overlay2, so two independent caps are double-counted or
mutually violable). Defaults are measured and env-settable (decision 6): 20 GiB total,
5 GiB of it the BuildKit cache share (the existing `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP=5GB`, promoted to one
place instead of duplicated), leaving a 15 GiB image/layer share that S5 sub-divides.

### The cap is enforced by Docker's OWN GC, at the source
The script renders the daemon's native BuildKit GC policy (`builder.gc`, `defaultKeepStorage`
plus a policy list) into `/etc/docker/daemon.json` by JSON MERGE, so the daemon refuses growth
on its own schedule rather than waiting for an external sweeper. `compose-up.sh` installs it
before starting Docker. `autodeploy.sh` derives its `--keep-storage` from the same script, so
prune and daemon GC cannot disagree about the cap. Nothing under `/var/lib/docker` is ever
deleted directly.

### Detecting the bytes `docker system df` cannot see
Two INDEPENDENT measurements of the same bytes, published as separate metrics:
- filesystem truth — `du -s` over `/var/lib/docker` and `/var/lib/docker/overlay2` (one `du`
  invocation, so overlay2's hardlinks are counted once);
- Docker's ledger — `docker system df` images + containers + build cache, human sizes parsed
  to bytes.

`docker_unaccounted_bytes` is overlay2 truth minus the ledger, clamped at 0. That delta IS the
orphan mass — 6.5 GB at the outage — and it is the one quantity no cap and no prune can reach,
because Docker does not know those bytes exist.

## Metrics (namespace `rebar/host`, dimensionless, 5-min probe)
`docker_storage_bytes`, `docker_storage_used_percent`, `docker_buildkit_cache_bytes`,
`docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent`, `docker_unaccounted_bytes`. Published only on a
successful measurement: a failed/timed-out probe publishes NOTHING and
`treat_missing_data = "breaching"` pages, following observability.sh 2e's gated-publish rule.

## Alarms — three, because one cannot answer for another
1. `rebar-docker-storage-cap-high` — the whole budget saturating.
2. `rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high` — the BuildKit GENERATOR at its own cap. BuildKit at
   100% of its 5 GiB share is invisible inside a 20 GiB budget reading 60%; a runaway image
   set saturates the budget while BuildKit sits at 10%. Neither alarm implies the other, which
   is the `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-debris` (3e92) argument: alarm on the generator, not only on
   aggregate fullness.
3. `rebar-docker-unaccounted-overlay2` — orphaned bytes above 2 GiB. Alarms 1 and 2 say "how
   full"; only this one says "full of what prune structurally cannot touch", and it changes the
   remediation from "prune harder" (the ~1.06 GB failure) to a daemon-level reclaim.

All three: `period=300`, `evaluation_periods=3`, `datapoints_to_alarm=2`,
`treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, both `alarm_actions` and `ok_actions` on
`aws_sns_topic.alerts`, and PINNED BY NAME in the watched set of
`tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py` (floors raised) so a later edit fails by name.

## Scope
In scope: host Docker/BuildKit config, prune integration, observability metrics, Terraform
alarms, runbook, tests. Out of scope: gate scratch volume (S1), journald (S3), `/var/tmp`
(S4), writable-container-layer sub-cap (S5). Terraform is written and validated only —
never applied.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single `/var/lib/docker` budget with an internal BuildKit/image split exists in one
      place, with measured, env-settable defaults and no duplicated constant.
- [ ] The BuildKit cap is enforced by the daemon's own `builder.gc` policy, merged
      idempotently into `/etc/docker/daemon.json`, and installed by `compose-up.sh`.
- [ ] `autodeploy.sh` derives its `--keep-storage` from that same budget; tagged rollback
      images (`:prev`, per-release mcp tags) are still never removed by a blanket prune.
- [ ] Observability publishes separate Docker storage, BuildKit cache and UNACCOUNTED
      overlay2 metrics, where unaccounted = filesystem `du` truth minus `docker system df`.
- [ ] Terraform declares the three alarms above, wired to SNS, all
      `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, all pinned by name in the alarm guard's watched set.
- [ ] The runbook documents per-generator diagnosis and remediation and forbids direct
      deletion under `/var/lib/docker`.
- [ ] Portability: everything runs from host config and local script tests; no CI-provider
      specific trigger is required.

## Testing
RED-first: each test below is written and observed failing before the implementation lands.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q tests/scripts/test_docker_storage_cap.py` —
  budget/split derivation, daemon.json GC-policy rendering, idempotent merge preserving
  pre-existing daemon keys.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q tests/scripts/test_observability_docker_storage.py`
  — metric emission over stubbed `docker`/`du`, human-size parsing, the unaccounted-bytes
  delta reproducing the incident's 16G-vs-9.5G shape, and silence (not a bogus 0) on probe
  failure.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py` — single
  budget drives `--keep-storage`; rollback images survive.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py` —
  the three alarms are present, actioned, breaching, and inside the raised floors.
- `terraform fmt -check -recursive infra/terraform` and
  `terraform -chdir=infra/terraform init -backend=false && terraform -chdir=infra/terraform validate`.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, plus `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py`,
  `tests/scripts/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py`, `tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py`.
